### edit1 vet-ticket NOT-gated bullet (insert before: "\n**If the payload or its target cannot be read, the write is")
- **The Notion practice page** (`NOTION_PRACTICE_PAGE_ID` in `~/.claude/hooks/auto-approve.js`) — a
  plain-text edit of it passes with no review. Anything else aimed at it is refused outright
  (`practice-page-plain-only`), and no review record can clear that refusal, so never run this skill
  for it: send a plain edit directly, or make the change in the Notion app.


### edit2 vet-ticket Step 1 non-zero exit
OLD:
**If it exits non-zero it prints no hash — then STOP and do not mint.** A non-zero exit means the
hook could not read that payload end to end, so it is going to hard-block the call whatever pass
exists. Re-issue the call in the ordinary shape instead of hunting for a pass.
NEW:
**If it exits non-zero it prints no hash — then STOP and do not mint**, and do what its message says:
no pass can help. The message names the cause — bad arguments, a payload file it could not read as
JSON, a fault in the gate itself, or a payload aimed at the Notion practice page (see the
practice-page bullet under "NOT gated").

### edit3 vet-ticket Step 2 guard paragraph (insert after: "er to sign off in its concluding report, not along the way.\n")

**The verdict-line guard (GEN-812).** `~/.claude/hooks/reviewer-verdict-guard.js` checks each ticket
reviewer's hand-back before it is delivered. If the last `TICKET-REVIEW-VERDICT:` in the report is
missing or malformed, or its hash is not one from the reviewer's prompts, it bounces the hand-back
back to the reviewer with instructions to re-send it ending with that line (at most twice per turn).
It checks form only; Step 7's `--ticket-verify` stays the authority, and Step 7 says what to do if a
report still arrives without the line.


### edit7 vet-ticket Step 7 no-token restatement
OLD:
`reviewer-unverified`, `bad-record`, `transcript-too-large`): re-review rather than mint.
NEW:
`reviewer-unverified`, `bad-record`, `transcript-too-large`): re-review rather than mint — except a
  `no-token` on a report that reads as a finished review: first SendMessage that same reviewer asking it
  to re-send its full report ending with the verdict block, token last, then re-run this check;
  re-review only if it still isn't `ok`.

### edit4 notion.md verdict-block bullet
OLD:
- **/vet-ticket reviewer sign-off can arrive without its verdict block.** Twice on 2026-10-11 a `check-reviewer` hand-back reached the caller as plain prose with no `TICKET-REVIEW-VERDICT` line, and `--ticket-verify` returned `no-token`. Always run `--ticket-verify` before minting; on `no-token` after a PASS-sounding report, SendMessage the same reviewer asking it to reply with only the filled verdict block (token last) and re-verify -- no re-review or re-hash needed.
NEW:
- **/vet-ticket reviewer sign-off can still arrive without its verdict block.** GEN-812's `reviewer-verdict-guard.js` bounces such hand-backs back to the reviewer, but it gives up after two bounces a turn and never sees plain-text delivery. Always run `--ticket-verify` before minting; on `no-token` after a report that reads as a finished review, follow /vet-ticket Step 7: ask the same reviewer to re-send its full report ending with the verdict block (token last) and re-verify -- no re-review or re-hash needed.

### edit5 notion.md staleness caveat (1)
OLD:
**(1) Sub-agents** — PostToolUse fires in the main session only and sub-agents can't run the REST check anyway, so don't delegate time-sensitive Notion reconciliation (reading current log/ticket state you'll write to or decide from) to a sub-agent; do it in the main session (or, if you must delegate, instruct the sub-agent to read via REST directly).
NEW:
**(1) Sub-agents** — hooks do fire inside sub-agents, but this warning then lands in the sub-agent's context, not yours, and a sub-agent has no shell to do the REST re-read it calls for, so don't delegate time-sensitive Notion reconciliation (reading current log/ticket state you'll write to or decide from) to a sub-agent; do it in the main session.

### edit6 wrap Step 3h (insert before: "## Step 4 — HISTORY.md\n")
## Step 3h — Verdict-guard readout (GEN-812)
`~/.claude/hooks/reviewer-verdict-guard.js` bounces ticket-reviewer hand-backs that lack their verdict
line and logs each decision. Run, from the Bash tool (where `$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` is readable):
`node "C:/Users/Erez/.claude/hooks/reviewer-verdict-guard.js" --readout "$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID"`
It prints nothing when there is nothing to report; otherwise relay each line it prints verbatim. If
`$CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` is empty, still run it (its other lines do not need the id) and add the line
`Verdict guard: this session's reviews couldn't be checked (session id unreadable)`. If the command fails
or prints "readout failed", say so in one line.
A `GEN-812 acceptance` line is a decision for Erez: put it in the "📌 For you" block as a proposal to
close (or reopen) GEN-812. Acting on his answer is a separate action, never part of this readout: only
on his explicit go, update GEN-812 per the ticket-status rules, then create the `.accepted` file the
line names, which retires the line.
**Traceability:** any line here counts as "a note the steps require surfacing", forcing the full Step 7
report, and each is recorded verbatim on its own line in the Step 4 HISTORY.md entry body. **The readout
is read-only:** it never writes the log or any marker file.
